correctness.rationale: For every N>=1 and positive sampler, normalized monomial testing gives a positive mixture of Poisson masses. The truncated Poisson width lemma follows by elementary Stirling bounds when intensity <=N and Gaussian product tails when intensity >N. Summation yields r>=A sqrt(N+1)/(3eB) without angular assumptions. Angular roots-of-unity diagonalize the finite sampler exactly; a nearest-integer Poisson lower bound and Gaussian-integral majorant prove all diagonal eigenvalues between 1/5 and 8. The proof includes quantifiers, positivity requirements, k=0 and N=1 boundaries, and explicit absolute constants. Replayed checker verifies 6369 finite assertions, used only as supplementary evidence.

originality.rationale: The focal claim is the optimal order of the number of distinct radii for uniformly conditioned positive Gaussian Fock polynomial sampling. Continuous trajectory sampling, exact Laguerre quadrature, and general MZ existence results are mathematically related but do not alone assert this unconditional finite radial-count lower bound alongside its finite construction. The 2019 general MZ framework, the 2021 polynomial Fock sampling paper, and the 2021 concentric Gabor-trajectory preprint were read and compared by implication. Source claims were checked in their mathematical statements, not by title; no inspected statement imposes the arbitrary-angle positive-weight lower bound. Published-result semantic searches and own-claim overlap checks yielded no matching claim. Residual unindexed or implicit-corollary risk remains; this is a best-knowledge self-review, not proof of absolute novelty.
residual_risks: Older Gaussian radial quadrature and approximate positive cubature literature may encode the same minimal radial complexity statement without those keywords.

value.rationale: The number of distinct sample radii is a natural structural resource for polar acquisition of Gaussian Fock polynomials, independent of the total angular sampling budget. The matched necessity and construction determine the optimal growth order Theta(sqrt N) in this positive weighted model; the lower bound prevents adding arbitrarily many angular points from compensating for too few radii. The scheme gives dimension-free numerical conditioning constants across an unbounded family of polynomial spaces. This is more than numerical conditioning at one fixed N or a generic restatement of existing MZ existence; it provides a quantitative geometric constraint usable in designing discrete Hermite/Gabor finite-subspace sampling.
